text:
Ari: Quick follow-up from the RFC — I sketched a minimal compatibility handshake for on-prem bundles to avoid forking agents. Want quick feedback before I add it to the proposal.
Mia: Awesome, send the sketch. main concern: how do we detect supported features without tight coupling?
Ari: Proposal: include a small top-level manifest.version + feature_flags array in the bundle header. Agents advertise supported_features on startup. If bundle has a flag agent doesn't support, we fall back to a compatible variant or fail-fast with a clear operator message.
Oliver: sounds reasonable. How do we express compatibility ranges? semver for manifest?
Ari: Yup, manifest_version follows semver-like integers (major.minor). Major bump = incompatible on-agent changes. Minor adds features agents can ignore safely.
Sanjay: What about live rollouts where older agents are still in fleet? We can't block activation across cluster.
Ari: Plan: staged activation with per-node precheck + optional conversion step. Steps: 1) agent downloads bundle header (no payload). 2) agent evaluates compatibility and reports status. 3) operator chooses rollout policy or automatic fallback variant.
Mia: That download-of-header idea is great — avoids wasting bandwidth. We should also sign headers separately so agents can verify before fetching payloads.
ops-bot: Note: RFC-466 posted to /docs/rfcs; link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/466
Oliver: How to handle older agents that refuse activation but can still serve? We need a compatibility shim that can transform older manifests into a subset older agents understand.
Ari: Proposal: support optional "compat_shims" directory in the bundle. Each shim is a small transformation script (WASM/binary) with metadata saying which manifest versions it can convert from->to. Agent operator can opt-in to run shim as part of staging.
Sanjay: Running arbitrary transformation on operator machines raises security questions. We should only allow verified WASM signed by our keys and run in sandbox.
Mia: Agreed. Also add resource limits and timeouts. In practice shims should be tiny (metadata remap, removing optional layers).
Oliver: Can you paste an example header snippet?
Ari: Sure:
```json
{
  "manifest_version": "2.1",
  "bundle_id": "modelstore-2026-03-10",
  "feature_flags": ["layer-deltas","meta-signed-index"],
  "shims": [
    {"name":"v2-to-v1-remap","from":"2.1","to":"1.9","sha256":"...","signed":true}
  ]
}
```
Sanjay: For rollout UX: agent should expose a preflight API: `/preflight-check?bundle=ID` that returns status, missing_support, estimated-extract-time. UI shows a per-node health map.
Mia: And a dry-run mode that simulates activation without touching the active image. critical for ops.
Ari: Exactly — preflight + dry-run + staged-activation window. Also automatic rollback token generated at preflight so operator can quickly revert.
Oliver: What about signature rotation and key escrow? If we sign headers separately we need key rotation flow that doesn't orphan old agents.
Ari: We attach key metadata to header: allowed_signers array plus grace_period window. Agents verify signatures against any signer in allowed_signers. Rotation process: publish new key in allowed_signers before removing old key after grace window.
Sanjay: One more: partial payload fetch (streamed chunks) for low-bandwidth sites. If agent supports resume tokens, preflight should also include available resumable ranges.
Ari: Agreed — header will include chunk map + optional resume token scheme. We will design chunk map to be compact and content-addressed so caches can serve repeated chunks.
Mia: TL;DR: manifest semver + feature flags, header-first signed preflight, optional signed WASM shims sandboxed, resume-aware chunk map, staged activation with dry-run + rollback token. Sounds good to put into RFC appendix. :+1:
Ari: I'll update RFC with these specifics and add a short operator UX mock for the Console. Ping me if you want to pair on the shim API.
Oliver: I'll review shim sanitization and WASM sandbox API.
Sanjay: I'll prototype the preflight API.
ops-bot: Reminder: please add RFC checklist items for security review and canary plan.
